categories.main_business_segments: Meiji Holdings operates two primary business segments: Food and Pharmaceuticals. The Food segment includes products such as yogurt, milk, beverages, cheese, butter, margarine, cream, ice cream, prepared foods, chocolate, gummies, sports nutrition, infant formula, liquid foods, beauty products, animal feed, sugar, and starches. The Pharmaceuticals segment covers prescription drugs, generic drugs, vaccines, and animal health products.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced fermentation, dairy processing, and food science technologies for its food products, including proprietary probiotic strains and functional food development. In pharmaceuticals, Meiji focuses on antibiotic production, vaccine development (including mRNA and inactivated vaccines), and biopharmaceutical manufacturing, with robust R&D in infectious diseases and biosimilars. Sustainability and digitalization are increasingly integrated into production and supply chain processes.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers for the Food segment are general consumers, retailers, foodservice providers, and B2B clients in Japan and overseas, with strong brands in yogurt, chocolate, and nutrition. The Pharmaceuticals segment serves hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, veterinarians, and government agencies, with a focus on infectious disease, immunology, CNS, and animal health markets. Major end markets include Japan, China, Southeast Asia, North America, and Europe.
categories.geographic_coverage: Meiji Holdings has a strong domestic presence in Japan and a growing international footprint, particularly in China, Southeast Asia (notably Vietnam and Thailand), North America (especially the US), and Europe. The company operates manufacturing and sales subsidiaries in these regions and is expanding its global supply chain and production capabilities.
categories.supply_chain_position: Meiji Holdings operates primarily as a downstream manufacturer and brand owner, producing finished consumer foods and pharmaceuticals. It also has midstream activities in ingredient processing and B2B food solutions, and is increasingly involved in upstream initiatives such as sustainable sourcing of raw materials (e.g., milk, cocoa, palm oil) and supplier engagement for environmental and social responsibility.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening core businesses, accelerating overseas growth, and creating new value in health and nutrition. R&D focuses on probiotics, functional foods, sustainable packaging, and digital health solutions in food, and on infectious disease, vaccines (including next-generation mRNA), biosimilars, and global product pipelines in pharmaceuticals. Sustainability, open innovation, and digital transformation are cross-cutting themes.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of consumer packaged goods (foods and beverages), B2B food ingredients, and pharmaceutical products (including prescription drugs, generics, and vaccines). Additional revenue streams include licensing, royalties, and contract manufacturing in the pharmaceutical segment.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In food, Meiji competes with other major Japanese and global food companies such as Morinaga, Yakult, and Nestlé, maintaining leading positions in yogurt, chocolate, and infant formula in Japan. In pharmaceuticals, it faces competition from domestic and international pharma companies, with a strong position in infectious disease and vaccines in Asia. Meiji is recognized for its integrated food and pharma business model and focus on health and wellness.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, Meiji Holdings reported consolidated sales of approximately 1.15 trillion yen, with operating profit of 84.7 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 50.8 billion yen. The company has over 17,000 employees and maintains a stable growth trajectory, targeting mid-single-digit annual profit growth and increased overseas sales ratio under its 2026 medium-term plan.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Meiji emphasizes high-quality, safe, and innovative products that deliver both taste and health benefits, leveraging proprietary technologies in probiotics and functional foods. In pharmaceuticals, its differentiation lies in infectious disease expertise, vaccine innovation, and reliable supply. The company positions itself as a 'food and health' leader, integrating sustainability, science, and customer-centricity to create unique value for consumers and society.
